summary: The new decomposition numbers are internally consistent with the generated diagnostic results, and the claims are wired into the replication runner and claim checker. The central defect is interpretive: middle-initial agreement—observed for only about one-fifth of added and dropped links—is used to suggest recovery of true matches, although the code supplies neither ground truth nor validation for the remaining four-fifths.

findings.title: Agreement with another transcription is used to infer recovery of true matches
findings.what_the_code_does: The diagnostic defines validation as literal initial agreement: `gen byte vb_`src' = mi1930_old==mi_`src'` and `gen byte va_`src' = mi1930_new==mi_`src'`. Here `mi_src` is extracted from an Ancestry or FamilySearch transcription, not a verified identity or hand-labeled ground truth. The paper nevertheless calls this link “quality” and says the result suggests the model is “recovering true matches rather than creating spurious ones.”
findings.why_it_matters: Two noisy transcriptions can agree on an incorrect initial, and disagreement can reflect transcription rather than linkage error. The reported agreement rates therefore do not identify the false-match rate or establish that the added links are true; this overstates what the new decomposition demonstrates.
findings.how_to_check: For added and dropped links, merge the link pairs to the independent genealogical reference standard used later in the paper and tabulate verified, contradicted, and unverifiable outcomes by `status`. Compare those results with `tab status va_anc` and `tab status va_fs` to show whether middle-initial agreement predicts independently verified links.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe these results strictly as middle-initial agreement, not accuracy or proof of true matching. Base the true-versus-spurious claim on the independent genealogical validation, ideally reporting its added-link and dropped-link results directly in this paragraph.

findings.title: The added-versus-dropped comparison omits roughly 80 percent of links without disclosing the resulting selection
findings.what_the_code_does: For each status, the code first counts all links as `nl`, but `summarize `3'_`src'` computes the reported agreement mean only where the validation variable is nonmissing. The generated results show initial coverage of only 20.5% and 19.2% for Ancestry added and dropped links, and 20.8% and 18.6% for FamilySearch. The paper reports 82–85% versus 71% “of cases” and immediately generalizes to the quality of the new links.
findings.why_it_matters: About four-fifths of added and dropped links cannot enter this validation comparison. Availability of a middle initial is plausibly selective by naming practice, nativity, transcription quality, and record legibility, so agreement among the observed fifth need not represent all added links—the population underlying the true-match claim.
findings.how_to_check: Run `tab status if congruent==0` and, for each source, `tab status if congruent==0 & !missing(va_anc)` or the corresponding before/FS variable; then compare race, nativity, literacy, name commonness, and legibility between links with and without usable initials.
findings.suggested_fix: State the approximately 20% coverage next to the 82–85% and 71% rates, label the comparison as conditional on usable initials, and add balance or independent-validation evidence showing whether evaluated and unevaluated links differ.

verified_clean.item: The new target-sample decomposition numbers match the generated results.
verified_clean.evidence: The diagnostic defines total, link, and reading components additively at replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do:120-138. Generated values are 18.2 total, 10.3/7.9 using Ancestry, and 8.4/9.8 using FamilySearch at replication/results/validation_fixed_initials.tex:97-103, supporting the arithmetic stated at paper lines 549-550.

verified_clean.item: The fixed-initial comparison actually holds the 1940 comparison initial constant across old and new links.
verified_clean.evidence: Ancestry and FamilySearch initials are constructed once per 1940 `id_B` at replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do:20-29, then used in both before and after indicators at lines 74-79.

verified_clean.item: Blank initials do not inflate agreement through Stata's `""==""` semantics in the new diagnostic.
verified_clean.evidence: Both fixed-source indicators require the 1930 and 1940 initials to be nonempty at replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do:76-77; the own-file indicators impose the same restriction at lines 39-40.

verified_clean.item: The added and dropped numerical claims are correctly mapped to both comparison sources.
verified_clean.evidence: The registry checks Ancestry and FamilySearch added-link rates and FamilySearch's dropped-link rate, plus an assertion for Ancestry's dropped-link rate, at replication/claims.toml:382-390. These correspond to 81.5/70.6 and 85.4/70.9 in replication/results/validation_fixed_initials.tex:44-49 and 84-89.

verified_clean.item: The new diagnostic is included in the machine-A replication sequence.
verified_clean.evidence: replication/run_machineA.do:95-105 runs `validation_fixed_initials.do`, and the four new claims cite that script at replication/claims.toml:363-389.

verified_clean.item: The all-record statement that most of the validation-rate increase reflects changed readings passes for both fixed sources.
verified_clean.evidence: The generated decomposition gives reading/link components of 1.093/0.057 for Ancestry and 0.629/0.521 for FamilySearch at replication/results/validation_fixed_initials.tex:90-96; the registry tests both inequalities at replication/claims.toml:392-397.

review_limits: The external data were not available in the repository, and the Stata pipeline was not rerun. Runtime quantities were checked against the committed generated result file rather than independently recomputed.

The review target was the tracked `git diff HEAD` in this repository plus the corresponding uncommitted paper edits. The untracked generated review prompt was not substantive analysis code and does not appear in `git diff HEAD`.
The review cannot determine from source alone whether missing-middle-initial selection is empirically benign; that requires the proposed balance and independent-validation tabulations.
